purpose: D6 correction ground: the six swallow-block keylog entries of the committed r58 receipt against the page-side keylog, matched BY VALUE (existence), never positionally.
extraction: jq key, cancelable, defaultPrevented per entry from .journey.form.swallowLeg; page side = .journey.form.pageKeylog scanned for equal-valued entries.
matchKey: (key, cancelable, defaultPrevented) equality over journey.form.pageKeylog entries
strictMatchKey: (key, code, cancelable, defaultPrevented, ctrlKey) equality, for multiplicity disclosure

aggregate.valueUniqueness: 3 of 6 keys match more than once by value: the control digits 7 and 5 and the Control modifier. Backspace, b and Enter carry a unique (key,cancelable,defaultPrevented) triple in the page keylog because only their keyDowns carry defaultPrevented=true; their keyUp twins carry defaultPrevented=false.

findings.detail: F1: the page keylog records defaultPrevented=false for the swallowed Backspace but the counter stayed green (predicate=true)

maskabilityTest.what: Measured emulation of a D1-style rule: every swallow-block entry (key,cancelable,defaultPrevented) must have an equal-valued page-keylog entry. Run on in-memory clones of the committed receipt (no lane bytes mutated, no file written outside scratch).

cases.case: forge pageKeylog[12] (control digit 5, one of 14 equal-valued twins) defaultPrevented false->true

maskabilityTest.finding: The existence-by-value rule catches a contradicted SWALLOW (Backspace, Enter: red) but is masked for the non-unique control entries (7, 5, Control: still green, because an equal-valued twin survives). Honest consequence for the r59 counter generation: the D1 check as specified protects exactly the entries the claim's witness rests on (the swallowed keys), and cannot, by itself, assert the non-swallow control entries' flags. A counter that also matched per-window occurrence counts, or that matched the keyDown only, would be strictly stronger.

notes: D6 ground: the r58 one-off cross-check (corpus/knowledge/chromium-preventdefault-swallow-round-58.md, section 'Cross-check of page record against driver block') reports 6/6 equal-valued matches. This receipt re-derives that result from the committed bytes by existence-by-value over journey.form.pageKeylog and confirms all six.

Not positional: the page keylog interleaves keyDown/keyUp pairs and the swallow block occupies indices 126..137, so a positional matcher sits one off-by-pair away from a silent pass. The existence test above is index-independent by construction.

Uniqueness caveat (honest): the value triple is not unique for the control digits 7 (6 matches), 5 (14 matches) and the Control modifier (4 matches). Only the swallowed Backspace (index 130), b (132) and Enter (135) carry a unique triple, because their keyDowns alone carry defaultPrevented=true. A per-entry existence check therefore detects a forge on a swallow entry but can be masked by a surviving equal-valued twin on the non-unique control entries.

The r58 sentinel evidence file exists and parses (sentinelEvidence above). Its F1 leg (page keylog forged to say the swallowed Backspace was NOT prevented) exited 0 with predicate true, which is the live proof that the r58 counter read the recorded block and not the page: the routed D1 defect the r59 counter generation must close.
